question: A 25-year-old man is brought to the emergency department 30 minutes after he was involved in a motorcycle collision. He was not wearing a helmet. Physical examination shows left periorbital ecchymosis. A CT scan of the head shows a fracture of the greater wing of the left sphenoid bone with compression of the left superior orbital fissure. Physical examination of this patient is most likely to show which of the following findings?

options.ope: Complete loss of vision of the left eye

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Fracture of the greater wing of the left sphenoid bone" -> "Compression of the left superior orbital fissure" -> "Involvement of cranial nerves passing through the superior orbital fissure" -> "Damage to the ophthalmic division of the trigeminal nerve (V1)" -> "Numbness of the left cheek" -> 85%

CHAIN: "Fracture of the greater wing of the left sphenoid bone" -> "Compression of the left superior orbital fissure" -> "Involvement of cranial nerves passing through the superior orbital fissure" -> "Damage to the abducens nerve (CN VI)" -> "Impairment of left lateral rectus muscle" -> "Impaired left lateral gaze" -> 70%

CHAIN: "Fracture of the greater wing of the left sphenoid bone" -> "Compression of the left superior orbital fissure" -> "Involvement of cranial nerves passing through the superior orbital fissure" -> "Damage to the ophthalmic division of the trigeminal nerve (V1)" -> "Absent left corneal reflex" -> 80%

CHAIN: "Fracture of the greater wing of the left sphenoid bone" -> "Compression of the left superior orbital fissure" -> "Involvement of cranial nerves passing through the superior orbital fissure" -> "Damage to the optic nerve (CN II)" -> "Complete loss of vision of the left eye" -> 75%

CHAIN: "Fracture of the greater wing of the left sphenoid bone" -> "Compression of the left superior orbital fissure" -> "No direct involvement of the olfactory nerve (CN I)" -> "Preserved sense of smell" -> 90%
analysis: The patient has a fracture of the greater wing of the sphenoid bone with compression of the left superior orbital fissure. This anatomical location affects the structures passing through the superior orbital fissure, which include the oculomotor nerve (CN III), trochlear nerve (CN IV), abducens nerve (CN VI), and the ophthalmic division of the trigeminal nerve (CN V1). The absence of the left corneal reflex suggests damage to the ophthalmic division of the trigeminal nerve, which is responsible for sensation to the cornea, and possibly the facial nerve if reflex arc is considered. This aligns with the injury described and the anatomical structures likely to be affected by the compression.
